articles.headline: Man City punishment must be 'three to five years' - Jamie Carragher
articles.description: Manchester City should face a multi-year punishment for their financial misdemeanours, according to former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・シティへの罰則は「3年から5年」であるべきだ ─ ジェイミー・キャラガー
articles.descriptionJa: リバプールの元ディフェンダー、ジェイミー・キャラガーは、マンチェスター・シティが財務上の不正行為により、数年間にわたる罰則を受けるべきだと述べている。
articles.body:
Manchester City should face a multi-year punishment for their financial misdemeanours, according to former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher.

An independent commission found City guilty of breaking Premier League rules in a strongly-worded report released last week, which the club have appealed against.

City were found to have inflated revenue by more than £830 million ($1.08 bn) over a nine-season period between 2009-10 and 2017-18 and, if their appeal fails, Carragher believes the sanctions should reflect that.

Speaking on The Overlap Fan Debate with Sky Bet, the 48-year-old said: "If the people talk about [a penalty of] 80 points or 100 points, but that's just over one season that gets you relegated and then you come back again.

"And I think players, a few of them would leave, but I think some of them would say, 'I could put up with that for a year.'

"But I think, because this has gone on for so long, I do think the punishment should be over a number of years, three to five years, and then players would move on."

City return to action this weekend when they take on Liverpool, arguably their biggest rivals for titles over the last decade and a half, in the Premier League on Sunday.

- Erling Haaland injury fear, asked to be substituted for Norway

- Transfer rumors, news: Haaland wants LaLiga move over Arsenal

- Kevin De Bruyne nets 200th career goal to lead Belgium past Turkiye

Enzo Maresca's side can expect a hostile atmosphere at Anfield, and former City defender and manager Stuart Pearce feels the Italian needs to try to use that in his favour.

"The opposition, they'll be rolling their sleeves up," Pearce said. "The atmosphere in the stadiums is going to be red hot. It's unbelievable it happens to be Liverpool this weekend. It's going to be electric.

"So it's going to stimulate everybody else against City, and it's got to stimulate City against everyone else."

articles.headline: Mourinho already has a lot to do to save Real Madrid's season
articles.description: It's only October, but Real Madrid already face a potentially season-defining run of five games that ends with El Clásico. What does José Mourinho need to get right?
articles.headlineJa: ムリーニョ、レアル・マドリードのシーズンを救うための課題は山積み
articles.descriptionJa: まだ10月に過ぎないが、レアル・マドリードはシーズンの運命を左右しかねない5試合の連続戦に直面している。その最後にはエル・クラシコが控えている。ジョゼ・ムリーニョに求められる正解とは何か？
articles.body:
At least Kylian Mbappé is laughing.

LaLiga is back this week, and the prognosis is already looking bleak for Real Madrid. After seven games, they trail leaders Barcelona by six points, with a high-stakes Clásico to come at Camp Nou on Oct. 25.

Barça's record so far is played seven, won seven. They've got a +24 goal difference, they've got Lamine Yamal, and they've got Raphinha in career-best form. From a Madrid point of view, this could get ugly.

- Who most deserves the Ballon d'Or? Whittling down the 30-man short list

- Portugal, Man Utd, Madrid:  Ronaldo's long history of rows with coaches

- Clásico match ball for Barcelona vs. Real Madrid LaLiga clashes unveiled

But Mbappé looked carefree enough on Sunday as he posted a self-recorded video on social media, smiling while riding a bike in what looked like an idyllic country setting.

There was just one problem: his manager José Mourinho had mentioned cycling in an interview 10 days earlier, citing it as a specific example of the kind of hobbies footballers must not undertake, given their responsibilities.

"You cannot ride a bike," Mourinho said, categorically. "You fall off, and maybe you don't play three matches, or maybe worse, you break a leg ... There are a lot of things you have to give up to be a football player."

Was Mbappé unaware of Mourinho's comments? Was this just an unfortunate coincidence? Or was there some other, as-yet unknown intent behind Mbappé's post, a message being sent? We'll hear Mourinho's response on Friday, as he speaks to the media the day before Madrid's game with Villarreal at the Bernabéu (stream LIVE 10/10 at 3 p.m. ET on ESPN+ in the U.S.).

In the meantime, Mbappé's off-field activities might not even rank among Mourinho's biggest worries this week as he works with his players on the training pitches at Valdebebas.

Mourinho has only been back at Madrid for three months. Now he has a run of five games -- Villarreal (home) on Saturday, AS Roma (away) on Oct. 14, Sevilla (home) on Oct. 18, RB Leipzig (home) on Oct. 21 and then Barcelona (away) four days later -- to get Madrid's season back on track, or risk derailing his project entirely.

So, what's the Real Madrid's to-do list ahead such a potentially season-defining set of fixtures?

Find Vinícius Júnior's best form

In eight Real Madrid games this season, Vinícius Júnior has scored just one goal, a close-range tap-in against Real Sociedad on Aug. 26. And when you look at the numbers, it gets even worse.

Take his personal, expected goal tallies against Espanyol (0.04 in 90 minutes), Málaga (0.04 in 90 minutes), Inter Milan (0.1 in 87 minutes), Rayo Vallecano (0.15 in 89 minutes) and Atlético Madrid (0.06 in 54 minutes).

Vinícius hasn't been scoring goals; he hasn't even looked like scoring goals. He's struggled to get into dangerous positions, and he's failed to convert on the rare occasions that he has.

articles.headline: Man City mock draft: How Premier League teams could pick in hypothetical punishment
articles.description: Now that Manchester City have been found to have cheated on a huge scale, anything is on the table -- maybe even an American-style Premier League draft?
articles.headlineJa: マン・シティ模擬ドラフト：仮定の制裁として、プレミアリーグの各チームはどう指名を行うか
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティの大規模な不正が判明した今、あらゆる可能性が浮上している。アメリカンスタイルのプレミアリーグ・ドラフト導入さえ、あり得るのだろうか？
articles.body:
Nearly a week after the Premier League found Manchester City guilty for 114 of the initial 115 charges brought against the club, it feels as if we're waiting to step across some new frontier.

So damning was the language in the league's redacted report that it really feels as if any punishment is suddenly on the table. The extent to which Man City were found to have broken the rules is unprecedented, and so too will likely be the punishment.

If you asked most reporters, say, two weeks ago about the possibility of Manchester City being relegated, we would've laughed it off. Well, as of today? Man City's relegation odds on DraftKings currently sit at plus-170, which implies odds of about 37%.

Do I think Manchester City are going to get relegated now? Well, I'd say there's something like a one-in-three chance that it actually happens. The team that has won six of the past eight Premier League titles might literally get kicked out of the Premier League. We'd be foolish to rule out transfer bans, stripping of titles, or, really, anything else.

Given that sense of prevailing uncertainty -- of what the punishment might be, of what the league will look like after it happens -- I want to do a little thought experiment. To be clear, I don't actually think that the Premier League is going to eliminate the existence of Manchester City and make all of their players available in an American-style expansion draft, but what, well ... what if they did?

I created the draft order based on the number of collective points that each club has won over the past four full seasons. And I broke the tiebreaker between Hull City and Coventry City based on Championship points over the same stretch.

Rather than trying to put myself inside the minds of each club's specific decision-makers, I made each pick as if I were running each club, based on what I think they should do, while occasionally hewing closer to the modus operandi of a couple of teams.

As for player contracts, consider this an imagined reality in which each team is able to afford and sign whomever they select.

With that, Hull City are now on the clock ...

1. Hull City: Erling Haaland, striker

He's the best goal scorer in Premier League history, and you don't even have to worry about the system fit. Although Haaland plays for a dominant possession team, he barely ever touches the ball -- he already plays as if he's on a counter-attacking, bottom-half-of-the-table team.

The fit and the need is so obvious that I'd say Haaland might be worth more than twice as much to Hull as any other player on this list.

Oh, and in case you were worried it was a Pep Guardiola thing ...

He already has nearly a full expected goal ahead of the player in second -- and the current season is five games old.

2. Coventry City: Rayan Cherki, attacking midfielder

We're quickly approaching a point at which it's not inappropriate to wonder whether Cherki is actually the best player in the Premier League.

articles.headline: How top Premier League clubs view Man City's guilty verdict
articles.description: Four clubs -- Arsenal, Liverpool, Man United and Tottenham -- retained their legal rights in the Premier League's case against Man City. Now that a guilty verdict has been issued, what will they do in response?
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグのトップクラブはマンチェスター・シティの有罪判決をどう見ているか
articles.descriptionJa: アーセナル、リヴァプール、マンチェスター・ユナイテッド、トッテナムの4クラブは、プレミアリーグによるマンチェスター・シティへの訴訟において法的権利を保持していた。有罪判決が下された今、彼らはどのような対応に出るのか。
articles.body:
Manchester City's guilty verdict on 114 breaches of Premier League rules, confirmed officially last Tuesday, is only the end of the beginning, with the appeals process and sanctions process to follow.

City continue to vehemently protest their innocence, and so any idea of a settlement is a fantasy right now. However, what comes after all this is potentially even more complicated because the ramifications of City's guilt stretch far and wide, as the purposeful inflation and misstatement of financial revenue by more than £900 million over a nine-year period (2009 to 2018) creates all sorts of alternative timelines.

What did these crimes cost other teams? City's rivals could have won titles, avoided relegation, qualified for the Champions League or signed many of those players who ended up at City. It adds up to potentially tens of millions in merit payments, and every club affected might look to find grounds to pursue compensation. The possibilities are almost endless, especially considering that prior to City's takeover by Abu Dhabi United Group in 2008, their best Premier League finish was eighth in 2004-05.

The independent commission set up to hear the case between City and the Premier League did not include compensation for wronged parties within the scope of its judgment. In September 2024, only four clubs instructed lawyers to inform City that they had reserved their right to seek compensation should they be found guilty: Arsenal, Tottenham, Liverpool and Manchester United. This was to ensure they had options beyond the six-year statute of limitations from the time the allegations were first published by Der Spiegel until the Premier League's verdict.

Sources have suggested to ESPN that City's aggressive denials hint at a major fight should any compensation case by brought, and it is debatable how many clubs would have the stomach for such a prolonged battle.

- Ogden: How Man City player exodus would warp transfer market

- Dawson: Man City players, staff react to guilty verdict

- Olley: Legal explainer of Man City's guilty verdict, next steps, more

All clubs will likely wait until the sanction is confirmed before deciding if, and how, to pursue a compensation case against City. ESPN reports on the mood at these four clubs and the reasons they all might yet seek individual retribution against City.

Arsenal

You could forgive former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger for taking City's wrongdoing more personally than most.

While the Gunners self-financed their move from Highbury to Emirates Stadium, the club was limited by terms of bank loans to spending 50% of its turnover on wages, essentially capping its ability to attract or retain talent based on money the club was bringing in. With the club's commercial revenue dwarfed by many of its rivals, Arsenal were effectively forced to offload many of their top players to comply with the financial rules of the time. articles.headline: Boos rain down from Superdome stands in Saints' blowout loss
articles.description: New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough understood the fans' frustration after the 1-3 Saints dropped a 45-24 decision to the Atlanta Falcons on Monday night, telling reporters after the loss that "we had some opportunities that we didn't take advantage of."
articles.headlineJa: セインツが大敗、スーパードームのスタンドからはブーイングが降り注ぐ
articles.descriptionJa: 月曜の夜、1勝3敗となったセインツがアトランタ・ファルコンズに24-45で敗れた後、ニューオーリンズのクォーターバック、タイラー・ショウはファンの不満を理解していると述べ、敗戦後の記者団に対し「活かせるチャンスがいくつかあったが、それをものにできなかった」と語った。
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS -- Quarterback Tyler Shough understood the fans' frustration after the New Orleans Saints' 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons.

The Saints were booed several times throughout the blowout loss, including going into halftime and at the end of the game. Saints fans left in droves before the end of the fourth quarter, leaving only Falcons fans in red jerseys in the stands.

"Fans understandably are upset," Shough said. "We had some opportunities that we didn't take advantage of and you're playing the Falcons and you lose like that. I mean, I'd boo, too. That sucks."

The Saints (1-3) went into the primetime game with a lot of emotion. The franchise was celebrating the 20th anniversary of the return to the Superdome after Hurricane Katrina forced them to play on the road the entire 2005 season.

Former Saints safety Steve Gleason, who famously blocked a punt to help beat the Falcons in that game in 2006, was honored during the game and in attendance with several other key figures, including Drew Brees and Roger Goodell.

But that emotion was quickly snuffed out after the Saints fell into a 24-7 deficit to their rival by halftime, turning cheers from the home crow to boos.

"I'm disappointed. More than anything, you lose the Falcons like that and especially on a Monday night game, it sucks," Shough said. "There's nothing you can say., like, 'Ah man, it doesn't suck.' It definitely does. But I do know as a team that we're extremely close and we're going to keep going and keep our eyes forward. We have really good leadership and our leadership on the team admits that we got to get better. We have to get better and watch the film and evaluate that. There's no hiding that. But at the same time, it is a long season and there's a lot of games yet to be played to where we can do that."

Saints defensive end Cameron Jordan said the team got "punched in the mouth early" and that the Falcons "had their way today." The Falcons rushed for 205 yards and five touchdowns between Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr.

"Everybody gets punched in the mouth in this game. Any given Sunday. But it's how you respond," Jordan said. "So we lost this game. Trash ass birds, they beat us, it is what it is. We have to be able to respond. That'll show you what type of team we are. We could go on for days ... about what we could do better. Break down the film, head to next week, we have to be a better team. Or this is what we'll get each and every week."

articles.headline: Resurgent Falcons score 80 points in two-game winning streak
articles.description: The 2-2 Falcons had a combined 16 points, the lowest total in the NFL, through two weeks, but after a 45-24 victory over the rival New Orleans Saints on "Monday Night Football," Atlanta now has a league-high 80 combined points in a two-game winning surge.
articles.headlineJa: 勢いを取り戻したファルコンズ、2連勝で合計80得点を記録
articles.descriptionJa: 2勝2敗のファルコンズは、最初の2週間でNFL最少となる合計16得点にとどまっていたが、マンデー・ナイト・フットボールで宿敵ニューオーリンズ・セインツに45-24で勝利。この2連勝の中で、アトランタはリーグ最多となる合計80得点を記録している。
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS -- The Atlanta Falcons' offense has completed an improbable turnaround in the span of just two weeks.

Over the first two games of the season, the Falcons had a combined 16 points, the fewest in the NFL. After a 45-24 win over the rival New Orleans Saints on "Monday Night Football," Atlanta had a league-high 80 combined points in Weeks 3 and 4.

The Falcons defeated the Green Bay Packers 35-14 at Lambeau Field last week on "Thursday Night Football." Atlanta is the first team in NFL history to win back-to-back primetime games on the road by 20 or more points, according to ESPN Research.

The biggest reason? Michael Penix Jr.'s return from ACL surgery.

The Falcons started third-string quarterback Cooper Rush the first two weeks of the season. Penix came back in Week 3 and led the Falcons to a dominant performance against the Packers. On Monday, Penix went 15-of-20 passing for 223 yards and a touchdown with no interceptions.

"He's been phenomenal, man," Falcons running back Brian Robinson Jr. said of Penix. "It ain't really much other words I can say about the way he's been playing. I appreciate his attitude, how he come in and just take the field and he's focused and he's ready. He's not letting nothing that he's been through in his past get in the way of his goals and what he wants in the future."

Penix, who tore his left ACL last November, is now the first Falcons quarterback with a completion percentage of least 70% and 10 yards per attempt in consecutive games since Matt Ryan in 2018.

Penix's presence has opened up things for the Falcons' running game in a huge way. Atlanta has gone over 200 yards on the ground in each of the last two weeks. On Monday, the Falcons had five rushing touchdowns. Bijan Robinson had 19 carries for 145 yards, and two touchdowns and Brian Robinson Jr. had 62 yards on 14 carries with three touchdowns.

"I feel like it could be the best in the league this year," right tackle Jawaan Taylor said of the team's ground attack.

The Falcons started 0-2 with a feeble offense and three straight primetime games coming up, two of them on the road, including Monday when the Saints were celebrating the 20-year anniversary of the first game back at the Superdome after Hurricane Katrina.

Atlanta has now won two straight heading into a date with the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday Night Football.

"We just want to show the world who we can be," Falcons safety Jessie Bates III said. "The first two weeks were not up to our standards. Obviously, when you got [Penix] back there dealing, it's a whole different team. So, we're just excited to continue to go with this."

articles.headlineJa: 代表ウィークによるプレミアリーグ選手の負傷への懸念
articles.descriptionJa: 2026-2027クラブシーズンの最初の代表ウィーク中に発生した、プレミアリーグのスター選手たちの負傷に関する最新ニュースとアップデートをお伝えします。
articles.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

articles.headline: Bijan Robinson powers Falcons past Saints 45-24 on the 20th anniversary of the Superdome's reopening
articles.description: — Bijan Robinson ensured there would be no punt to block this time — and the Atlanta Falcons were off and running.
articles.headlineJa: ビジャン・ロビンソンが牽引し、ファルコンズがセインツに45-24で勝利。スーパードーム再オープン20周年記念日に。
articles.descriptionJa: ビジャン・ロビンソンが145ヤード前進し2タッチダウンを記録。ファルコンズは月曜夜の試合でニューオーリンズ・セインツに45-24で圧倒的な勝利を収め、スーパードーム再オープン20周年を祝う雰囲気に水を差す形となった。
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS -- — Bijan Robinson rushed for 145 yards and two touchdowns, and the Falcons posted a dominant 45-24 victory over the New Orleans Saints on Monday night, dampening celebrations commemorating the 20th anniversary of the Superdome's reopening after Hurricane Katrina.


              Brian Robinson ran for three short touchdowns for the Falcons (2-2), who never trailed and controlled the line of scrimmage while outgaining the Saints (1-3) on the ground, 207 yards to 50.


              Atlanta continued rolling behind quarterback Michael Penix Jr., who returned to the lineup for a 35-14 victory at Green Bay. Penix was an efficient 15 of 20 for 223 yards and a touchdown. His 31-yard scoring strike to Jahan Dotson in fourth quarter sent Saints fans toward the exits en masse.


              Saints running back Alvin Kamara scored his first two touchdowns of the season, the second cutting Atlanta's lead to 31-17 early in the fourth quarter.


              Tyler Shough passed for 286 yards and a late touchdown to Devaughn Vele.


              The game kicked off following festivities commemorating the Saints' return to the Superdome after Katrina had displaced the team from New Orleans for the entire 2005 season. In addition to causing levee breaks and a storm surge that flooded about 80% of the city, the hurricane also ripped a hole in Superdome’s roof while evacuees sheltered there.


              Ignited by Steve Gleason’s punt block for a touchdown following the 2006 game’s opening possession, the Saints beat the Falcons 23-3 in that Week 3, Monday night matchup.


              Like that meeting two decades ago, the Falcons, wearing red, received the opening kickoff. This time, however, there would be no punt to block. Bijan Robinson burst through a hole on the left side of the line and raced 59 yards for a touchdown.


              For a fourth time in four games, the Saints were playing from behind early — a challenge made more difficult by Daniel Carlson’s missed 52-yard field goal attempt and running back Kendre Miller’s lost fumble on the New Orleans 22-yard line one possession later.


              Atlanta cashed in on the turnover when Bijan Robinson made it 14-0 on a 4-yard power run, set up in part by cornerback Kool-Aid McKinstry’s third-down defensive holding penalty.


              Pregame ceremonies feature 2006 Saints players
              Wearing white jerseys, retired players Drew Brees, Scott Fujita, Scott Shanle, Deuce McAllister, Devery Henderson and Curtis Deloatch joined Gleason on the field before kickoff to lead fans in the club’s familiar “Who dat!” chant. Gleason, using a wheelchair because of ALS, was joined by his son, Rivers, who raised his father's arm and then pulled it down to signal the start of the chant.


              Irma Thomas, a New Orleans native and resident who sang the national anthem when the dome reopened, returned to perform it again.


              NFL Commissioner Roge

articles.headline: Atlanta's jabs at New Orleans after MNF top Week 4 trolls
articles.description: The calendar shifted to October, and the trolls are becoming a little more impactful, led by the Atlanta Falcons.
articles.headlineJa: MNFが第4週の煽り合戦の舞台となる中、アトランタがニューオーリンズを揶揄
articles.descriptionJa: 10月を迎え、アトランタ・ファルコンズを中心としたネット上の煽り合いは、より激しさを増している。
articles.body:
Welcome to the first weekend of October, when the games get a little more meaningful and the trolls follow suit. Week 4 of the NFL season was further proof of that.

The Atlanta Falcons dominated the New Orleans Saints 45-24 on "Monday Night Football," thanks to a standout performance from their backfield.

Atlanta put up a whopping 420 yards, led by 145 rushing yards by Bijan Robinson, who also added two scores. His fellow running back Brian Robinson Jr. put up three touchdowns. The Falcons' five rushing touchdowns tied a franchise record. They are the sixth pair of teammates who each had multiple rushing touchdowns in a "Monday Night Football" game. The Falcons' lone passing touchdown occurred when quarterback Michael Penix Jr. connected with wide receiver Jahan Dotson for a 31-yard score. 

With the Falcons-Saints rivalry being one of the fiercest in the league, it only made sense that Atlanta poked fun after the victory -- multiple times. The Falcons captioned their post: "Marched in," a nod to the Saints' anthem, "When the Saints Go Marching In."

The Falcons then resurfaced a video in which a Saints fan motioned a choking sign at Falcons players as they entered halftime with a lead, indicating that Atlanta would eventually lose. The original video had the caption: "This Saints fan potentially could have an all-time clip for the second half," to which the Falcons quipped postgame with: "He did not." 

 

Here are the other top trolls from Week 4.

Dallas Cowboys 34, Houston Texans 30

The Dallas Cowboys defeated the Houston Texans on the road. Facing a four-point deficit with 2:23 left, Dallas went on an 11-play, 74-yard drive that concluded with a 12-yard touchdown catch by wide receiver CeeDee Lamb.

It put the Cowboys up for good and capped a stellar performance from Lamb. He had a whopping 17 catches -- second most in franchise history -- for 189 yards. It's the most receptions by any player since Keenan Allen had 18 in Week 3 of the 2023 season, according to ESPN Research.

Dallas had clever jabs lined up for the in-state matchup. The Cowboys referenced country star Ella Langley's hit track, "Choosin' Texas," in a social media post, adding "Dallas" ahead of "Texas."

Then, Dallas put a spin on the opening sequence from the sitcom "King of the Hill," which is set in Texas. The illustration featured Lamb, Dak Prescott, wide receiver George Pickens and safety Caleb Downs hanging out together with "Kings of the State" written above them.

Carolina Panthers 32, Detroit Lions 26 

It required one final stop, but the Panthers survived for a "Sunday Night Football" win against the Lions.

Carolina held a six-point lead when Detroit regained possession with 2:06 left. Four plays later, the Lions turned it over on downs, clinching the Panthers' victory. articles.headline: 76ers backup center Ariel Hukporti exits preseason opener early
articles.description: Just five minutes into the preseason opener against the Knicks on Monday, 76ers backup center Ariel Hukporti suffered a right leg injury, causing him to leave the game.
articles.headlineJa: 76ersのバックアップセンター、アリエル・フクポルティがプレシーズン開幕戦で途中退場
articles.descriptionJa: 月曜日に行われたニックスとのプレシーズン開幕戦において、76ersのバックアップセンターであるアリエル・フクポルティが開始わずか5分で右脚を負傷し、試合を離脱した。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- Just five minutes into the preseason opener against the New York Knicks on Monday, 76ers backup center Ariel Hukporti suffered a right leg injury, causing him to leave the game.

The non-contact injury occurred with 7:06 remaining in the first quarter. Hukporti fell to the floor on the defensive end and immediately grabbed his lower right leg.

The big man, signed to a one-year, $3.4 million free agent contract in July after winning a championship with the Knicks, was helped off the floor during an ensuing timeout.

The Sixers confirmed at halftime that Hukporti would not return.

Hukporti started against his former team with Philadelphia already thin in its frontcourt rotation.

Joel Embiid, who missed 150 games over the last three seasons because of various injuries, has been healthy during training camp but given the night off by Sixers coach Nick Nurse, along with LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey, who were also healthy scratches.

Philadelphia was also without two of its backup centers in Adem Bona and Tacko Fall.

Bona, in his second season with the team, has yet to participate in training camp after suffering a left foot sprain during the offseason while playing for Turkey's national team.

Last week, a Sixers spokesman said that Bona would be reevaluated imminently, and Nurse told reporters he hoped Bona would be available at some point during the preseason.

The 7-5 Fall, signed to an Exhibit 10 training camp deal with a chance to compete for a two-way roster spot, was diagnosed with a left hip sprain after undergoing an MRI last Wednesday. The team said he would be reevaluated in about two weeks.

Before the Knicks game, Nurse said he hoped to have the majority of his players available to play together in two out of the Sixers' three remaining preseason games. Philadelphia goes on the road to play the Brooklyn Nets on Thursday, followed by the Boston Celtics on Saturday before closing the exhibition schedule home against Boston on Oct. 16.

The season opener is Oct. 20 in New York against the Knicks.

articles.descriptionJa: ボーンマスのアレックス・スコットは、シャビ・アロンソ率いるチームへの移籍を実現できるか？最新の移籍情報を伝える。
articles.body:
Chelsea lead the race for AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, while Bayern Munich are bracing for tough contract talks with star winger Michael Olise. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Chelsea are leading the race to sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, who is also attracting strong interest from Liverpool and Arsenal, as reported by The Telegraph. Elsewhere, TEAMtalk have suggested that Real Madrid are considering becoming involved in the race for the 23-year-old after watching him closely in recent weeks. Los Blancos have watched Scott at least three times, including his first England start in the Three Lions' 7-0 victory over Croatia.

- Bayern Munich are concerned about talks to renew Michael Olise's contract, as the winger hasn't yet told them if he even wants to stay in Bavaria, as reported by Sport Bild. The Bundesliga club is preparing for a very difficult negotiation with the representatives of the 24-year-old. One of the sticking points is that the France international wants a release clause in his new contract, something both Harry Kane and Jamal Musiala have. Bayern are willing to offer a mega contract that will run until 2032 but want an answer by next summer.

- Italian outlet Corriere dello Sport has offered an insight into the names Roma are looking at as they aim to sign a winger. In the summer, they looked at Stuttgart's Jamie Leweling and Chelsea's Jamie Gittens, who have both had a lack of game time since the summer transfer window shut so could be available for less than was demanded before. They also want Real Madrid's Endrick, hoping for a Donyell Malen-style deal where they have a loan with the option to make it permanent, and they aren't alarmed by AC Milan's interest. Frosinone's Giorgi Kvernadze is another player of interest.

- Juventus see Marseille midfielder Pierre-Emile Højbjerg as the leader Luciano Spalletti needs, as reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport. They have previously looked at Leon Goretzka and Franck Kessié, who ended up at Aston Villa and Atalanta respectively, but remain keen on signing an older head for their midfield so are turning to the man who is captain for both Marseille and Denmark. There have already been exploratory contacts made about the 31-year-old, while Teun Koopmeiners is the main candidate to leave so he can come in.

- Juventus have recently made a move for Frosinone goalkeeper Lorenzo Palmisani and Inter Milan are monitoring him, as reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport. Inter chief executive Beppe Marotta has insisted on a mix of foreign and Italian players, emphasizing the importance of a strong Italy squad. I Nerazzurri could decide to loan out the 22-year-old if they sign him, and they are also looking at Alessandro Romano, who is on loan at Cagliari from Roma.

articles.headline: State of each position in 2026: What are the biggest tactical trends?
articles.description: Elite soccer has changed dramatically in recent years, and the most valued player skill sets have evolved as a result.
articles.headlineJa: 2026年の各ポジションの現状：最大の戦術的トレンドとは？
articles.descriptionJa: エリートサッカーは近年劇的な変化を遂げており、その結果、最も価値の高い選手のスキルセットも進化している。
articles.body:
Elite European soccer in 2026 feels decidedly different from what we've become used to. Over the past couple of seasons, the Premier League has been increasingly characterized by direct attacking, set pieces and long throw-ins. Many encounters between big clubs across Europe have become frenetic, end-to-end affairs, such as the Bayern Munich-Paris Saint-Germain semifinals in last season's UEFA Champions League.

A lot of the changes seem related to how teams play without the ball. The soccer we became accustomed to throughout the 2010s involved top sides trying to push their opponents back while keeping the ball. Once the ball reached the attacking third, they tried to outnumber defenders in key spaces and make use of their attacking talent.

One way for defensive sides to counter this approach is to use zonal marking, which involves defending space rather than individual players. They would set up in compact blocks and deny space in critical areas, whether they defended deep like Max Allegri's Juventus in the 2010s or pressed high like teams coached by Ralf Rangnick's disciples. While this tactic helps protect the areas closer to goal and prevent mismatches, it sometimes plays into the hands of those high-possession sides.

As a result, player marking (or man-to-man marking), in which defenders are assigned to follow attackers around up and down the pitch, started to make a comeback at the turn of the 2020s. Teams like Mikel Arteta's Arsenal and Andoni Iraola's Bournemouth combined this concept with their zonal marking, switching out of a zonal structure in certain situations to swarm teams attempting to move the ball forward (hybrid pressing). This makes moving the ball slowly up the pitch harder, causing teams to embrace more direct approaches with the ball.

Meanwhile, the game appears to be becoming more physical and more intense. Since the COVID-19 pandemic, every passing season of the Premier League has seen faster sprinting and more "high-intensity actions." And with off-ball physical data like running distance or top speed becoming more accessible, scouting departments now possess more transparent measures of athleticism, leading to players' athletic qualities being valued more.

Rather than just affecting the head coach's team talk, these big-picture changes have a major effect on the skill sets that clubs look for when assembling their starting XIs. Let's take a look at five positions -- goalkeepers, center backs, fullbacks, central midfielders, and strikers -- to see what has changed and why.

Goalkeepers: Distribution and cross-claiming

New Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki has generated much buzz this season. One of his standout features has been his passing ability, playing quick passes to his center backs during the early buildup and exquisite floated long passes to Villa's forwards to escape pressure.
